payout_quote: Through weatherization improvements and upgrades, these households save on average $372 or more every year according to a national evaluation of the program.
timing: No fixed payout — free weatherization services are scheduled after application approval; state-agency waitlists of several months are typical; savings accrue as lower energy bills.
eligibility: Household income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (DOE WPN 22-5). Priority given to the elderly, persons with disabilities, and families with children. Renters are eligible with written permission from the landlord. Undocumented households follow HHS LIHEAP guidance referenced by DOE.
catches: This pays $0 in cash — you receive free home improvements and lower bills, not money. It is savings, not income.
Income-restricted: at or below 200% of the federal poverty line. An average user above that line gets nothing.
State-administered with limited slots (~32,000 homes/year nationally per DOE) — waitlists of months are normal.
Renters need written landlord permission before any work.
DOE publishes no per-home dollar figure; the route's '$1,000-$10,000+' describes the value of free services, not a payment.
steps: Confirm your household income is at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (check the current HHS poverty guidelines table).
Go to the official DOE page https://energy.gov/wap and open the 'how to apply' page to find your state's WAP administrator.
Contact your state's WAP office or local community action agency and complete the application with income documentation.
A certified auditor performs a home energy audit to determine the most cost-effective improvements.
Approved improvements (insulation, air sealing, HVAC, etc.) are installed at no cost to you by the agency's contractors.
biggest_catch: This pays $0 in cash — it is free home improvements and lower bills, not money earned — and only households at or below 200% of the poverty line qualify, with months-long state waitlists.
notes: Verified against the live DOE WAP page 2026-09-22 (program active: 8,500 jobs, ~32,000 homes/year, news updates through July 2025) and DOE WPN 22-5 for the 200% FPG income rule. PRODUCT NOTE: WAP is cost savings for low-income households, not a way to make money — it should never be presented as income. The $10,000 top end is not a DOE-published figure.
